extraction_method: manual (ads-dna skill invoked but its fixed output schema did not match the Phase 0 Step 5 schema required by PLAN.md; extraction process followed the skill's methodology — homepage + subpages via WebFetch, plus raw-HTML curl+grep for colors/fonts since WebFetch strips CSS — but output was written to this custom schema instead)

visual_identity.color_source_note: WebFetch strips CSS, so colors were pulled from the raw homepage HTML (curl) — the two primary blues (#005EFF, #009BEC) come from fill attributes inside the embedded Interview Kickstart logo SVG at https://interviewkickstart.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/620b3b133ad9178175a0f3bb_interviewkickstart-logo-1.svg; the light-blue secondaries and neutrals come from inline CSS on the homepage (background/text colors). No official brand style-guide document was found on the site, so this is a reverse-engineered palette, not a stated one — recommend visual confirmation against the live site before locking creative.

typography.note: No Google Fonts / custom @font-face import was found on the homepage. CSS shows only the browser system-font stack (-apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica Neue, Arial, Noto Sans) and a long list of unused WordPress/Elementor theme font-preset utility classes (Inter, Poppins, Montserrat, etc. are available as presets in the theme but no evidence any specific one is the applied heading/body font). Cannot ground a specific typeface without a screenshot/visual check — left null rather than guessed.

visual_identity.imagery_style: Blue-toned vector iconography and illustrated graphics on the homepage (rocket/skills imagery), combined with real headshot photography for instructors and student testimonials, plus a horizontal scrolling strip of recognizable tech-company logos (Amazon, Apple, Atlassian, Cisco, GitHub, Google, LinkedIn, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle, Uber, Walmart, Adobe). Clean, product-marketing / SaaS-style layout (WordPress + Elementor site), not editorial photography-led.

attributes: credential-heavy (FAANG+/MAANG+, Tier-1 mentors named by company)
urgency and momentum-driven imperative CTAs ("Turbocharge", "Pivot", "Book", "Join Next Webinar")
AI-era relevance framing ("Now Powered by AI", "Decode the 2025 Playbook")
do: lead with concrete, sourced numbers (salary, hikes, offers, instructor counts) — never invented ones
reference real named companies only where the site itself names them (testimonials, mentor bios, logo strip)
use short, imperative CTAs matching the site's own button copy (e.g. "Book FREE Webinar", "Join Next Webinar")
frame messaging around career transformation / AI-skills relevance, matching homepage section headers ("Pivot to AI with Precision", "Upskill with Intent")
dont: fabricate or round statistics beyond what a specific page states (the site's own stats are inconsistent across pages — see claims_guardrails)
state or imply a guaranteed job/salary outcome — no formal guarantee/refund policy was found anywhere on the site
use generic corporate stock-photo tone; site favors real instructor/alumni photos and company logos over generic imagery
mention or compare against named competitors — none appear anywhere on the site

requires_verification: Learner-count figure is inconsistent across pages: homepage says '25,000+ Tech Professionals', /in says '27,000+ professionals trained', /about-us says '13,500+ experienced engineers trained', /courses says '20,000 engineers... secured offers'. Pick one figure (with as-of date) and confirm with the marketing/data team before use in any ad.

Average salary hike figure is inconsistent: /courses says '66.5% Average salary hike', homepage says '60%+ Increase in salaries', /about-us says '₹23 LPA average salary hike' and '60% average salary increase', /in says '₹24 LPA Average salary hike'. Confirm the current, approved figure before use.

Highest-offer figure differs by market framing ($1.2M globally vs ₹1.7Cr on the India page) — confirm which currency framing to use for India-targeted creative and whether these represent the same underlying case or two different ones.

The phrase 'guaranteed success' appears once on the homepage ('...our flexible, personalized paths for guaranteed success') — this reads as marketing copy, not a formal guarantee/refund policy (none was found on the cost/FAQ page). Do not repurpose this phrase as a guarantee claim in ad copy without explicit legal/marketing sign-off.
No pricing (INR or USD) is published anywhere on the site — the cost guide page explicitly defers to a webinar/advisor call. Do not state or imply specific pricing in ads.
claims_guardrails.notes: Salary/placement claims must be used verbatim from the site with the source cited above; no fabricated stats; no competitor mentions; no guarantee language beyond what the site itself uses (and even the site's one 'guaranteed success' phrase should be treated cautiously — see requires_verification).
